speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) when did the Ministry became aware of Grab Holdings’ decision to cut 1,000 jobs or 11% of its workforce, given Grab Holdings’ statement in September 2022 that it had no plans to undertake mass layoffs; (b) what proportion of those jobs that are cut are held by Singaporean workers; and (c) whether the Ministry is engaging with Grab Holdings with a view to facilitate the transition of displaced workers into suitable jobs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned that the proportion is the same before and after the layoff.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share a bit more about the proportion of those jobs were lost by Singaporean workers?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second supplementary question is a bit broad.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Grab's decision to conduct a layoff is an indication of more widespread trouble lurking in the tech sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what processes are there in MOM to mitigate the risks of this going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Also, what are the forward-looking processes that MOM intends to take going forward as well?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is to be fair to the firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I also alluded to it in my answer that the profiles before and after are the same.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, if you work backwards, proportionally, whether it is Singaporeans or other profiles, they remain largely the same.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Basically, there is no one group that was affected more than another.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, they came up with similar profiles before and after.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is demand and I think beyond the sector, we have also found that tech skills are still going to be in high demand even in non-tech firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To a large extent, we are at almost full employment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, opportunities remain high in terms of a vibrant information and communications (I&C) market.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But at the same time, we do have to also prepare for a slowdown that could come.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I would just say that we are cautiously optimistic about long-term prospects for the I&C sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But at the same time, there is demand even beyond the sector for tech skills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As a whole, what MOM is doing is, as I have shared, we are working closely with WSG and e2i.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is most critical for us, especially to ride on the current demand and vacancies within the I&C sector as well as the broader economic requirements.
